name: Osmany Juantorena
milestone_by_age_26: Won CEV Champions League gold with Trentino Volley in 2009/10 and 2010/11, plus FIVB Club World Championship gold in 2009 and 2010, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Juantorena began playing volleyball at Orientales de Santiago in Cuba from age 12, joining the Cuban national team at 18 in 2003 and winning Pan American Games silver that year. He moved to Russian club Ural Ufa in 2004 but received a two-year doping ban in November 2006, missing the 2007-2009 seasons before joining Trentino Volley in 2009.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Santiago de Cuba.
primary_early_advantage_tags: national team pipeline, physical edge, adversity (doping ban), club system
evidence_summary: Juantorena started volleyball young in Cuba's state sports system, joining the national team at 18 and winning Pan American Games silver in 2003. His career was disrupted by a two-year doping ban in 2006, but he returned with Trentino Volley in 2009 and immediately won multiple CEV Champions League and FIVB Club World Championship titles before age 26. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Santiago de Cuba; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Playing for Vero Volley Monza in Italian Serie A as of 2024-25 season; multiple CEV Champions League and FIVB Club World Championship winner with Trentino Volley.

trajectory.event: Won Pan American Games silver medal with Cuban national team.
Won FIVB World League bronze medal with Cuba.
Received a two-year doping ban while playing for Ural Ufa, sidelining his career.
Returned from ban with Trentino Volley, winning CEV Champions League gold and FIVB Club World Championship gold.
Won second consecutive CEV Champions League gold and FIVB Club World Championship gold with Trentino.
Won Olympic silver medal with Italy at the Rio de Janeiro Olympics.

name: Franck Ribéry
milestone_by_age_26: Was a France international and key player at the 2006 FIFA World Cup where France finished runner-up; joined Bayern Munich in 2007 for a club-record fee, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Ribéry began playing football at age six at FC Conti Boulogne, then joined Lille's academy in 1996 but was released due to academic and behavioral problems. He worked his way through lower-division French clubs (Boulogne, Alès, Brest, Metz) before breaking through at Galatasaray and Marseille in 2005, earning a France call-up and World Cup spot in 2006.
family_context_summary: Born in Boulogne-sur-Mer and raised in a low-income neighborhood on the fringes of the city. His father worked as a construction worker, and Ribéry himself worked in construction with his father before turning professional.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a construction worker, not in football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: low-income background, car accident scars, lower-division grinding, direct domain exposure
evidence_summary: Ribéry grew up in a low-income family in Boulogne-sur-Mer, suffering severe facial scars from a car accident at age two. He was released from Lille's academy and clawed his way through lower-division French football before breaking through at Galatasaray and Marseille in 2005. His World Cup 2006 performances earned him a move to Bayern Munich for a club-record fee. His father was a construction worker, and Ribéry worked in construction before turning professional.
starting_point: Born to a low-income family in Boulogne-sur-Mer, France; father was a construction worker; suffered severe facial injuries in a car accident at age two.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2022; last club was Salernitana; serves as technical collaborator at Salernitana.

trajectory.event: Made senior debut for US Boulogne in the French lower divisions.
Broke through at Galatasaray and then Marseille, establishing himself in Ligue 1.
Was a key player for France at the FIFA World Cup, scoring a goal and helping France reach the final.
Joined Bayern Munich for a then club-record fee of 25 million euros.
Won the treble with Bayern Munich and was nominated for the FIFA Ballon d'Or alongside Messi and Ronaldo.
Left Bayern Munich after 12 seasons with 9 Bundesliga titles and a Champions League trophy.

name: Abbas Kiarostami
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Kiarostami's first film 'The Bread and Alley' was made in 1970 at age 30. Before age 26, he was studying painting and graphic design at the University of Tehran and making TV advertisements, with no material filmmaking milestone.
early_history_summary: Kiarostami majored in painting and graphic design at the University of Tehran, supporting his studies by working as a traffic policeman. Between 1962 and 1966, he shot around 150 advertisements for Iranian television and began creating credit titles for films in the late 1960s. His first film was made in 1970 at age 30.
family_context_summary: Born in Tehran to a Persian family. His first artistic experience was painting, winning a competition at age 18.

name: Ondrej Nepela
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in men's singles at the 1972 Sapporo Winter Olympics at age 21, along with three World Championship titles (1971-1973) and five European Championship titles (1969-1973), all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Nepela began skating at age 7 in 1958 after watching the European Championships on television. His mother brought him to a Bratislava ice rink where coach Hilda Múdra took him on. He competed at the 1964 Olympics at age 13, won his first European Championship bronze at 15 in 1966, and rose to dominate European and World figure skating from 1969 to 1973.
family_context_summary: Born in Bratislava, Czechoslovakia. His mother was a housewife and seamstress, and his father was a chauffeur. They were from central Slovakia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were a housewife/seamstress and a chauffeur, not in skating.
primary_early_advantage_tags: dedicated coach Hilda Múdra, early specialization, compulsory figures mastery, state sports system
evidence_summary: Nepela was born to a working-class family in Bratislava and started skating at age 7 after watching the European Championships on TV. His mother connected him with coach Hilda Múdra, who became his lifelong coach and described him as diligent and punctual. He competed at the 1964 Olympics at age 13, won European bronze at 15, and dominated from 1969-1973 with five European titles, three World titles, and Olympic gold in 1972. His success was built on early specialization and a sustained coach-athlete relationship within the Czechoslovak state sports system.
starting_point: Born in Bratislava, Czechoslovakia to a working-class family; mother was a housewife and seamstress, father was a chauffeur.
current_position: Died on February 2, 1989 at age 38 in Mannheim, West Germany, from AIDS-related illness; final role: professional skater and coach.

trajectory.event: Began skating under coach Hilda Múdra at Slovan Bratislava after watching the European Championships on television.
Competed at his first Winter Olympics in Innsbruck, placing 22nd.
Won his first European Championship bronze medal in Bratislava.
Won his first European Championship gold medal, beginning a five-year reign.
Won his first World Championship gold medal in Lyon.
Won Olympic gold medal in men's singles at the Sapporo Winter Olympics.
Won his third World Championship title in Bratislava and retired from amateur competition.
Died of AIDS-related illness in Mannheim, West Germany.

name: Talant Duyshebaev
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold with the Unified Team at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at age 24, becoming the tournament's top scorer with 47 goals; won World Championship gold with Russia in 1993 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Dujshebaev started playing handball relatively late at age 14, having previously practiced swimming. He joined CSKA Moscow's youth system and progressed to the senior team in 1985 at age 17. He won the IHF Junior World Championship with the Soviet Union in 1989 and became a senior national team player before the Soviet Union's collapse, leading to his Olympic and World Championship triumphs in 1992-1993.
family_context_summary: Born in Frunze, Kirghiz SSR, Soviet Union (now Kyrgyzstan). Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CSKA Moscow system, Soviet sports pipeline, national team, late starter but rapid rise
evidence_summary: Dujshebaev was born in the Kirghiz SSR and started handball at age 14, later than most elite players, after switching from swimming. He joined CSKA Moscow, one of the premier Soviet sports clubs, and progressed rapidly through the Soviet national team pipeline. He won the IHF Junior World Championship in 1989, then Olympic gold in 1992 as the tournament's top scorer, and World Championship gold in 1993, all before age 26. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Frunze, Kirghiz SSR, Soviet Union (now Kyrgyzstan); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Head coach of the France men's national handball team as of 2025; widely regarded as one of the greatest handball players and coaches of all time.

trajectory.event: Joined CSKA Moscow senior team, beginning his professional handball career.
Won IHF Junior World Championship gold with the Soviet Union.
Won Olympic gold with the Unified Team at Barcelona, finishing as tournament top scorer with 47 goals.
Won World Championship gold with Russia and signed for Spanish club Teka Cantabria.
Won Olympic bronze with Spain at Atlanta and was named MVP of the European Championship.
Won second Olympic bronze with Spain at Sydney.

name: Albin Vidović
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold with Yugoslavia at the 1964 World Handball Championship in Czechoslovakia at age 21, and Mediterranean Games gold in 1967 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Vidović played for RK Partizan Bjelovar from 1960 to 1975, starting at age 17. He joined the Yugoslav national team in 1963 and was part of the gold medal-winning team at the 1964 World Championship. He also won Mediterranean Games gold in 1967 and later Olympic gold in 1972.
family_context_summary: Born in Zagreb, Independent State of Croatia (during WWII). Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yugoslav national team, RK Partizan Bjelovar, team sport system
evidence_summary: Vidović was born in Zagreb during WWII and joined RK Partizan Bjelovar at age 17 in 1960, where he spent his entire 15-year club career. He entered the Yugoslav national team in 1963 and won World Championship gold at age 21 in 1964. He also won Mediterranean Games gold in 1967 and Olympic gold in 1972. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources, and his Wikipedia article is very sparse.
starting_point: Born in Zagreb, Independent State of Croatia (during WWII); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on March 8, 2018 at age 75 in Bjelovar, Croatia; final role: retired handball player.

trajectory.event: Joined RK Partizan Bjelovar, beginning his senior handball career.
Debuted for the Yugoslav national team.
Won World Championship gold with Yugoslavia in Czechoslovakia.
Won Mediterranean Games gold with Yugoslavia in Tunis.
Won Olympic gold with Yugoslavia at the Munich Olympics.
Retired from competitive handball after 15 years at RK Partizan Bjelovar.

name: Drake
milestone_by_age_26: Debut album 'Thank Me Later' debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 in June 2010 at age 23, selling 447,000 copies in its first week; earlier, 'So Far Gone' mixtape (2009) produced the Platinum-certified hit 'Best I Ever Had' reaching #2 on the Billboard Hot 100.
early_history_summary: Drake began acting on Degrassi: The Next Generation at age 15 in 2001 to support his financially struggling family. He simultaneously pursued music, self-releasing mixtapes starting with 'Room for Improvement' in 2006 and 'Comeback Season' in 2007. His 2009 mixtape 'So Far Gone' went viral, leading to a deal with Lil Wayne's Young Money Entertainment and his 2010 debut album 'Thank Me Later' debuting at #1.
family_context_summary: Born in Toronto to an African-American drummer father from Memphis and a Canadian Ashkenazi Jewish mother who worked as an English teacher and florist. Parents divorced when he was five; father was incarcerated on drug charges. Raised by his mother in modest circumstances in Toronto.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a drummer who performed with Jerry Lee Lewis, providing some music industry exposure, but was largely absent after the divorce.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Degrassi acting platform, mixtape distribution, Lil Wayne co-sign, Toronto music scene, adversity
evidence_summary: Drake grew up in modest circumstances in Toronto with a single mother after his parents divorced when he was five; his father, a musician, was largely absent and incarcerated. He began acting on Degrassi at 15 to support his family, using that income to fund early music projects. His father's background as a drummer provided marginal music industry exposure. His self-released mixtapes built an online following, and Lil Wayne's co-sign in 2009 catalyzed his mainstream breakthrough. His debut album Thank Me Later debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 in 2010 at age 23.
starting_point: Born in Toronto to an African-American drummer father from Memphis and a Canadian Jewish mother who was an English teacher and florist; parents divorced when he was five; raised in modest circumstances by his mother.
current_position: One of the best-selling music artists of all time with over 230 million records sold; founder of OVO Sound record label; estimated net worth ~$250 million; resides in Toronto.

trajectory.event: Began acting as Jimmy Brooks on Degrassi: The Next Generation, providing financial support for his family.
Self-released debut mixtape 'Room for Improvement', selling roughly 6,000 copies.
Released 'So Far Gone' mixtape; single 'Best I Ever Had' reached #2 on Billboard Hot 100 and was certified Platinum; signed to Young Money Entertainment.
Debut album 'Thank Me Later' debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 with 447,000 first-week sales.
Released 'Take Care' album, later included on Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list.
Released 'Nothing Was the Same' and became global ambassador of the Toronto Raptors.
Released 'Views' which led the Billboard 200 for 13 weeks; single 'One Dance' became first song to surpass 1 billion Spotify streams.

name: Renée Colliard
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in women's slalom at the 1956 Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics at age 22, winning by a margin of over three seconds.
early_history_summary: Colliard was a pharmacy student at the University of Geneva who joined the Swiss national alpine skiing team shortly before the 1956 Winter Olympics. She became the surprise winner of the women's slalom by over three seconds and was also Swiss national champion in the slalom that same year. The 1956 Olympics were her only major international success.
family_context_summary: Born in Geneva, Switzerland. She was a pharmacy student at the University of Geneva. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swiss national team, alpine skiing access
evidence_summary: Colliard was a pharmacy student at the University of Geneva who joined the Swiss national alpine skiing team only shortly before the 1956 Winter Olympics. She became the surprise Olympic champion in women's slalom by a margin of over three seconds and was also Swiss national champion that year. Her Wikipedia article is very sparse with minimal biographical detail. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Geneva, Switzerland; was a pharmacy student at the University of Geneva; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on December 15, 2022 at age 88; final role: retired, having graduated in pharmacy in 1960 and run a ski resort and pharmacy in Montana, Valais with her husband.

trajectory.event: Won Olympic gold in women's slalom at the Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics by over three seconds; also Swiss national slalom champion.
Graduated in pharmacy from the University of Geneva.
Died on December 15, 2022 in Switzerland.

name: Haruki Murakami
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Murakami's first novel 'Hear the Wind Sing' was published in 1979 at age 30. Before age 26, he was a university student and jazz bar owner with no material writing milestone.
early_history_summary: Murakami studied at Waseda University in Tokyo and owned a jazz bar called Peter Cat for approximately seven years (circa 1972-1979) before publishing his first novel. He was heavily influenced by Western literature and music during his youth.
family_context_summary: Born in Kyoto, Japan. His father was the son of a Buddhist priest, and his mother was the daughter of an Osaka merchant. Both parents taught Japanese literature.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents taught Japanese literature, providing a literary household environment, though Murakami gravitated toward Western literature.

name: Michaëlle Jean
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: By age 26 (September 1983), Jean was a university student completing her BA at the University of Montreal and doing social work at a women's shelter. Her journalism and broadcasting career began after completing her MA around 1986, with no material journalism milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Jean fled Haiti with her family to Canada in 1968 at age 11 to escape the Duvalier regime. She grew up in Thetford Mines, Quebec, then Montreal. She earned a BA in Italian and Hispanic languages and literature from the University of Montreal and concurrently worked on spousal abuse research and at women's shelters from 1979-1987. She later completed an MA in comparative literature and taught Italian Studies before beginning her journalism career.
family_context_summary: Born in Port-au-Prince, Haiti. Her father was a principal and teacher at a Protestant school who was arrested and tortured under the Duvalier regime in 1965. The family fled to Canada in 1968, settling in Thetford Mines, Quebec. Her parents' marriage later fell apart due to her father's violence.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a school principal and teacher; family was politically persecuted under Duvalier, creating refugee adversity.

name: Rumiko Takahashi
milestone_by_age_26: Began professional manga career in 1978 at age 21 with first published work 'Katte na Yatsura' earning honorable mention at the Shogakukan New Comics Contest, followed by serialization of 'Urusei Yatsura' in Weekly Shōnen Sunday; won the Shogakukan Manga Award in 1980 at age 23 for Urusei Yatsura.
early_history_summary: Takahashi showed little interest in manga as a child but co-founded a manga club in high school. During university, she enrolled in Gekiga Sonjuku, a manga school founded by Kazuo Koike (Lone Wolf and Cub), and published her first dōjinshi in 1975. She worked as an assistant to horror manga artist Kazuo Umezu. Her professional career began in 1978 with her first published work and the serialization of Urusei Yatsura.
family_context_summary: Born in Niigata, Niigata Prefecture, Japan. Family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond her birthplace.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kazuo Koike manga school, Kazuo Umezu assistantship, Weekly Shōnen Sunday platform, Shogakukan contest
evidence_summary: Takahashi was born in Niigata and co-founded a manga club in high school with Yōko Kondō, who also became a manga artist. During university, she enrolled in Gekiga Sonjuku, the manga school of Kazuo Koike (Lone Wolf and Cub), who pushed students to create well-thought-out characters. She also worked as an assistant to horror manga artist Kazuo Umezu. Her professional career began in 1978 at age 21 with her first published work and the serialization of Urusei Yatsura in Weekly Shōnen Sunday. She won the Shogakukan Manga Award in 1980 at age 23. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Niigata, Niigata Prefecture, Japan; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: One of Japan's best-known and wealthiest manga artists with over 230 million copies in circulation; recipient of the Grand Prix de la ville d'Angoulême (2019) and Medal with Purple Ribbon (2020); still actively publishing manga.

trajectory.event: Published first dōjinshi creations while studying at Gekiga Sonjuku manga school under Kazuo Koike.
Professional debut with 'Katte na Yatsura' earning honorable mention at Shogakukan New Comics Contest; began serialization of 'Urusei Yatsura' in Weekly Shōnen Sunday.
Won the Shogakukan Manga Award for Urusei Yatsura; began serialization of 'Maison Ikkoku' in Big Comic Spirits.
Concluded both Urusei Yatsura (34 volumes) and Maison Ikkoku (15 volumes); began 'Ranma ½' series.
Began 'Inuyasha' series, which ran until 2008.
Received the Grand Prix de la ville d'Angoulême, becoming the second woman and second Japanese to win the prize.
Awarded the Medal with Purple Ribbon by the Japanese government for contributions to the arts.

name: Knut Johannesen
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic silver in 10,000m at the 1956 Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics at age 22; won World Allround Championship gold in 1957 at age 23; won European Allround Championship gold in 1959 at age 25; all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Johannesen was born in Oslo and represented the Aktiv SK skating club. He won the Norwegian Allround Championships starting in 1955 at age 21-22, won his first World Allround title in 1957, and became the dominant long-distance speed skater of his era. He worked as a carpenter during his competitive career.
family_context_summary: Born in Oslo, Norway. He worked as a carpenter and later ran a gas station alongside his skating career. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian skating tradition, Aktiv SK club, long-distance specialization, carpenter day job
evidence_summary: Johannesen was born in Oslo and represented Aktiv SK. He emerged as Norway's dominant speed skater starting in 1955, winning the Norwegian Allround Championships eight times between 1955 and 1963. He won his first World Allround title in 1957 at age 23, Olympic silver in 10,000m in 1956, and European Championship gold in 1959. He worked as a carpenter during his competitive career, indicating no significant family financial platform. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Oslo, Norway; worked as a carpenter during his skating career; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired former speed skater living in Oslo, Norway; two-time Olympic champion and former world record holder; age 92 as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Won his first Norwegian Allround Championship, beginning an eight-year domestic dominance.
Won Olympic silver in 10,000m at the Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics.

Won European Allround Championship gold in Gothenburg and received the Oscar Mathisen Award.
Won Olympic gold in 10,000m at Squaw Valley, setting a world record as the first man to break 16 minutes; named Norwegian Sportsperson of the Year.
Won Olympic gold in 5,000m and World Allround Championship gold, completing his collection of major titles.
